Everything reference-grade in one place. Supplier evidence is the structured body of documents, records, traceability logic and audit trails that lets a European buyer verify a supplier's claims — this Library defines the terms, answers the recurring questions, links the official sources and states our published positions.

Jump to: Glossary · FAQ · Official sources · Positions · Market · Publications

Reference material only — not legal advice. Regulatory facts should be checked against the current official texts (linked below) before decisions.

Glossary — the terms that decide contracts

Supplier Evidence

The structured body of documents, data, records, traceability logic, ownership controls and audit trails that allows a buyer, bank, auditor, legal team or board to verify supplier claims and assess exposure.

Buyer-Ready Evidence

Supplier documentation organised so that procurement, legal, compliance, customs, audit, finance and board teams can use it without rebuilding the supplier file from zero.

Board-Usable Evidence

Evidence structured for executive risk decisions — connecting claims, records, owners, audit trails, regulatory exposure, contract duties and financial consequences.

Regulatory Defensibility

The ability to connect a supplier claim, document, process, source, owner and audit trail to the regulatory or contractual risk the buyer needs to assess.

Evidence Conversion

Translating operational reality into documentation that buyers, banks, auditors and boards can read, test and defend.

Supply Chain Evidence Risk

The gap between what a buyer must verify and what the supplier can prove with reliable, current, controlled and traceable evidence.

Supplier Evidence File

A structured file containing the documents, records, claims, owners, audit trails and risk mappings needed to answer evidence requests — graded on the SEMM scale.

CBAM Evidence

The product, installation, emissions, methodology, carbon-price and document-governance records that support a buyer's CBAM import-risk analysis — see the CBAM Review.

EUDR Traceability Evidence

Commodity, origin, legality, geolocation, custody and document-governance records supporting deforestation-free and legal-production claims — see the EUDR Review.

Contract Clause Evidence Risk

The exposure created when a signed clause requests proof the operation cannot currently provide — see the Clause Review.

Audit Trail

The reconstructable path from a claim to its records: who produced them, when, under which scope, stored where, changed by whom.

P&L Exposure

The financial consequence of weak evidence: pricing pressure, delayed renewals, reduced volumes, harder financing — cost that arrives before any formal rejection.

FAQ — what executives ask first

Procurement asks: can the supplier be approved?

Approval hinges on whether the evidence file answers the buyer's screen without manual reconstruction. Operational quality alone does not approve a supplier — the file does.

Legal asks: can the supplier defend the clause?

A clause is defensible when every promised proof point maps to an existing, owned, dated record. Anything else is risk transfer accepted at signature.

Finance asks: can this affect P&L?

Yes — before any fine: through discounts under deadline pressure, renewal delays, conservative CBAM default values and financing conversations that stall on unverifiable claims.

Is any of this certification?

No. Advisory review with a published methodology. Certification and emissions verification are accredited activities performed by others — and we say so on every page.

Where do I start?

With the request you received: send it via the scope assessment. No request yet? Self-score with the gated executive materials there.

Published positions

Suppliers do not have an ESG problem

They have an evidence problem: real operations, fragmented files. The fix is documentation architecture, not marketing.

Buyers do not need claims

They need supplier evidence they can read, question, compare and archive. Everything else is friction priced against the supplier.

The request is the standard

When a European buyer asks for evidence, what happens next is decided by the file — not the operation. Prepare the file before the request defines the timeline.

The market context

EU regulation (CBAM, EUDR, CSDDD, CSRD, DPP) is converting supplier documentation into a market-access asset across EU–Brazil trade. The commercial consequence: buyers consolidate around suppliers whose evidence is cheap to use — and reprice the rest. That is the market this practice serves, and the reason the reference layer above exists.

html:
If your company buys from Brazil, European rules have quietly moved your suppliers' paperwork onto your desk: due-diligence duties under CSDDD, value-chain reporting under CSRD, embedded-emissions data under CBAM, traceability under EUDR. The questionnaires you send come back — in Portuguese, late, incomparable, and impossible to grade from Munich or Milan.

Villanova ESG works the other end of that problem: at origin. We review your Brazilian suppliers' evidence where it lives — in the language it was written, against the operation it describes — and return it in the structure your procurement, compliance and audit teams can actually use.

This is advisory work. It is not an audit, certification, legal opinion, emissions verification or a guarantee of buyer acceptance — and every deliverable states that boundary.

What we do for buyers

Per-supplier evidence assessment

Each supplier graded against the published SEMM framework: what exists, what is missing, what would not survive your review — with owner, date, scope and source per record. Comparable across the whole supplier base.

Is not: an audit, an EcoVadis-style self-declared score, or a site certification.

Pilot cohort

Start with a small set of critical suppliers — enough to test the method against your framework before extending it across the base. Scope, cohort and calendar defined in the scoping conversation.

Supplier development path

Assessment without a path breeds resentment. Each graded supplier receives a prioritised gap register in Portuguese — so your supply base improves instead of churning.

Why at origin — and why us

  1. Language and ground truth. Brazilian evidence is written in Portuguese, referenced to Brazilian instruments (MTR, CDF, licences). Reading it accurately is the work — translation alone loses the scope and the caveats.
  2. A published yardstick. The methodology is public, citable and deposited with DOIs — your committees can read exactly how a grade was produced. No black-box scoring.
  3. Operational lineage. The founder also leads Ecobraz, a documented Brazilian reverse-logistics operation serving corporate clients since 2011. Distinct organisations, declared relationship: it means the person grading a chain-of-custody record has actually run one.
  4. Boundary discipline. Deliverables state what each record proves and what it does not. If a statement cannot be verified, it is not written.

Where this fits your obligations

The assessments are designed to feed the processes the rules require of you — risk analysis and monitoring under CSDDD, value-chain information for CSRD, supplier data organisation for CBAM and EUDR — without pretending to replace them. Your legal duty, your assurance provider and your filings remain yours; our work makes the underlying supplier evidence usable inside them.

What buyers ask us first

Can you certify our suppliers? No — and be wary of anyone who says yes. We produce advisory assessments with a published methodology. Certification is a different, accredited activity.

Do you work in English? Deliverables are in English (or Italian on request); the origin work happens in Portuguese — that is the point.

What does it cost? Engagements are scoped case by case — cohort size, depth and calendar drive the work. The scoping conversation ends with a written proposal.

Make the scoping conversation count

To arrive at a proposal in one round, include five things in your message: your role, your country, the approximate number of suppliers in Brazil, the regulation or buyer requirement driving the request (CSDDD, CSRD, CBAM, EUDR, internal policy), and the deadline that matters. We reply within one business day with next steps and a calendar slot.
